findings.channel: active foreign intervention -> host institution capacity
findings.finding: Transfer is linear in foreign force contribution until clamp. It has transfer efficiency and crowding-out but no domestic administrative/integrity/legitimacy throughput gate.

findings.channel: foreign support package -> government training/organizational learning
findings.finding: Institution-capacity gain is invariant to support-package magnitude because T cancels. This channel cannot encode either dose response or absorptive saturation.
Financial aid does scale with package size, but its direct institutional-learning companion does not share the domestic state-regeneration absorptive-capacity function.

theory_implication: Foreign state-building currently has transfer/crowding-out concepts but is not coupled to the domestic absorptive-capacity architecture. This can make foreign institution-building structurally inconsistent with domestic rebuilding and cannot reproduce aid-volume saturation or implementation overload.
required_before_change: Freeze a synthetic mechanism contract comparing the current transfer law against an absorptive-throughput formulation.
Do not tune against Afghanistan outcomes; Afghanistan remains a conceptual comparator only.
Preserve a compatibility mode or explicit version gate because changing foreign transfer equations invalidates prior v2 foreign-affairs theory outputs.
guard: This is a source-level mathematical audit, not an empirical claim that foreign aid is ineffective or that a particular real-world aid function is correct.
